subject.title: Codex app-server client closes before long maintenance turn completes; Gateway restart also terminates active turn without graceful recovery

question: For Codex-backed turns interrupted by Gateway restart or app-server client close after possible side effects, should OpenClaw resume, synthesize a final status, or fail closed with restart-specific recovery guidance?
rationale: The remaining behavior crosses replay safety, transport failure classification, Gateway lifecycle, and channel delivery policy; source proves partial mechanisms exist, but not which product behavior maintainers want for side-effecting maintenance turns.

options.title: Design restart-aware recovery
options.body: Define a single policy for Gateway shutdown, unexpected app-server close, safe resume, and final user-visible follow-up, then implement it with focused regression coverage.

options.title: Limit to diagnostics and copy
options.body: Keep runtime behavior fail-closed but make logs and user-facing messages distinguish Gateway restart from unexpected app-server failure.

options.title: Wait for live reproduction
options.body: Keep the issue open under live-repro until a current-main run proves the remaining long-maintenance trigger before choosing recovery behavior.

recommendation.title: Design restart-aware recovery
recommendation.body: Define a single policy for Gateway shutdown, unexpected app-server close, safe resume, and final user-visible follow-up, then implement it with focused regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The current narrow Codex retry boundary and failure copy trace to their merged work, making them the best available owner for the cross-surface product decision.
